Shield Charge Paladin - Group Support Variant

block-and-thorns bruiser, aura-weighted

Paladin hybrid unchanged block-and-thorns bruiser, aura-weighted based on Shield Charge Thorns Paladin

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 14

Move on whenHerald of Zakarum equipped. Everything about this build's block chance assumes a shield off-hand.
Move on whenMaximum Resolve at 30 and block chance visibly past 80%.
Move on when100% block chance reached. That is the number this whole page is organised around and it is binary.

Skill bar

1Clash
2Shield Charge
3Defiance Aura
4Condemn
5Fanaticism Aura
6Fortress

Rotation

Unchanged from the base build: both auras up, Clash to build Resolve, Shield Charge through the pack so the hits count as blocks and Retribution pulses. In a party, position so the pulses land where other people are fighting rather than where you want to be.

Skill point priority

  1. Defiance Aura first, and further than the base build takes it - it is 50% bonus Armor and Resistances after 3.1.x and it is a party buff
  2. Fanaticism Aura second: it is where Vulnerable, Weaken and Fortify come from, and it gives 14% critical strike chance at 15 ranks
  3. Clash for Resolve generation, paired with Defiance Aura
  4. Shield Charge with Hit Count As Blocking, which is what turns driving through a pack into blocks
  5. Fortress for the Resolve damage bonus and Unstoppable
  6. Condemn last

6Fortress

Rotation

Auras up, Clash on cooldown, Shield Charge to reposition the whole party's fight rather than to reposition yourself. Condemn to gather. The measurement that matters here is not your damage - it is whether your block chance is climbing toward the Interdiction threshold.

Skill point priority

  1. Both auras maxed
  2. Resolve to 30: three +6 Maximum Resolve tempers - each has to crit and then Masterwork-crit to reach +6 - plus Aspect of Glynn's Anvil and the Phoba of Righteous Will charm set
  3. Block chance sources, and this variant wants all of them: Aegis at 42% at rank 15, the Castle and Shield Bearer paragon boards, Aspect of Interdiction (up to 100% with enough maximum Resolve) and Bulwark's Aspect
  4. Shield Charge and Clash kept where the base build has them

Rotation

Same loop. Aspect of Interdiction moves onto a ring here rather than waiting for the base build's push transfiguration, because block chance is this variant's primary output and it should arrive as early as the gear allows.

Skill point priority

  1. Unchanged; the character is finished in shape and unfinished in numbers
  2. Glyph level order, published by the base guide: Sentinel, Spirit, Honed, Outmatch, Revenge
  3. Keyword sources worth keeping in mind in a party, because they are things you provide: Vulnerable, Weaken and Fortify all come from Fanaticism Aura; Resolve from Defiance Aura plus Clash; Unstoppable from Defiance Aura

2Shield Charge
3Defiance Aura
4Condemn
5Fanaticism Aura
6Fortress

Rotation

Both auras up at all times - that is the job, and dying is the only way to fail at it. Clash on cooldown for Resolve, Shield Charge to reposition the fight, Condemn to gather. Solo, this is a slower version of paladin-meta-shield-charge and there is no reason to prefer it.

Skill point priority

  1. Everything maxed
  2. Blood-Mad Idol is deliberately not taken; see the tweaks
  3. At this point the honest framing is that you are not pushing, you are enabling three other people to push. Maxroll's push list rates Support zDPS Paladin S tier and says group play only, and this page does not claim otherwise

Board & glyph focus

Glyph level order, published verbatim and identical in all four variants: Sentinel, Spirit, Honed, Outmatch, Revenge. The class mechanics to understand here are the Juggernaut Oath, which is one of the three things Resolve scales damage through, and Resolve itself - baseline maximum 8, generated by Defiance Aura and Clash. Retribution is the Thorns pulse that fires on block.

How to run them

Identical across all four variants: hire Raheir, who 'grants you Bastion and Inspiration to buff your damage', and reinforce with Aldkin, who 'reduces enemy damage and slows with Field of Languish'. Note this is the opposite emphasis from most Season 14 builds, which take Raheir purely for survivability - here Inspiration is picked up as a damage node, which is the tell that this build already has its own defence covered by block, Resolve and Fortress and is spending the mercenary slot on offence and on the damage-reduction layer instead.

Plan

Activity-level advice re-weighted for group content, not a per-build allocation: no Paladin guide publishes War Plan picks and the base build's planner payload carries none. These are Maxroll's build-agnostic endgame progression priorities with five of the nine moved into Lair Bosses and The Pit, which is where a support Paladin is wanted. No `level` is recorded because no source publishes an order.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 5 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.

Summary

The class's best solo build, re-weighted toward the role the sources actually rate the class highest in. Maxroll's push list carries a Support zDPS Paladin in S tier, group play only - the only S-tier Paladin entry anywhere in this repo's tier data - while its best solo build, the Shield Charge base build, tops out at A. The 3.1.2 class snapshot says the same thing from the other direction: launch buffs 'didn't translate to Pit performance' but the class 'maintains group/Hardcore viability'. Rather than write a support build from nothing, this variant takes the Shield Charge shell that is fully sourced and moves its optional budget from personal damage to the two auras that 3.1.x buffed hardest: Defiance Aura's bonus Armor and Resistances went 30% to 50%, and Aegis now also grants 30% Armor while active. Resolve capping stays, because the cap is what drives Aspect of Interdiction toward 100% block chance, but the Juggernaut Oath damage payoff stops being the reason for it. Play the base build solo. Play this one when there are three other people relying on your auras.

Reasoning

Based onShield Charge Thorns Paladin
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. Defiance Aura and Fanaticism Aura are treated as the build's output rather than as support for it. 3.1.x took Defiance Aura's bonus Armor and Resistances from 30% to 50% and gave Aegis an additional 30% Armor while active, and neither number is worth more to you than to a party.
  2. Blood-Mad Idol is not recommended at the push stage. It is still drawn on the amulet row, because this variant inherits the base build's own planner payload for its gear model and that payload equips it - saying otherwise would misdescribe the page. What changes is the advice: the base guide is explicit that it 'makes surviving more of a challenge but damage gain is so significant that it is worth it', which is correct for a solo damage dealer and backwards for a character whose job is to still be standing. Wear a well-rolled Legendary amulet with Block Chance instead.
  3. Block chance is prioritised over critical strike damage on the amulet and rings at every stage. The base guide's own stat rule points this way for a low-crit character: 'if you have very low Critical Strike Chance, Physical Damage, Vulnerable Damage or All Damage multipliers have more value'.
  4. Resolve capping to 30 is kept in full - three +6 Maximum Resolve tempers, Aspect of Glynn's Anvil and the Phoba of Righteous Will charm set - but for Aspect of Interdiction's block chance rather than for the Juggernaut Oath damage. Same gearing, different reason, and it matters when you have to choose which Resolve source to drop.
  5. Aspect of the Indomitable stays on the chest into the endgame where the base build drops it after the levelling stage; a support character wants the block-scaled defensive line more than it wants the slot back.
  6. Adds a War Plans allocation the base build does not carry, weighted toward Lair Bosses and The Pit - the group content this variant exists for.
